subject: Urgent: ByteGrid enterprise feature exception — KV cache isolation + SLA routing
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ByteGrid: enterprise ask — KV per-tenant isolation + route-level SLA (initial)

Team — quick sync on an ask from a ~$1.2M ARR renewal/expansion (ByteGrid). They want two items to be contract-level commitments for Dedicated: 

1) Per-tenant KV/prefix isolation (no cross-tenant KV reuse) for prompt/cache privacy;
2) Route-level SLA: ability to set latency/throughput targets per route/model and fallback routing to a lower-cost model if SLA would be violated.

Why urgent: customer has regulatory auditors in June and procurement is pushing to finalize terms by 6/10. They explicitly said they will require a contractual callout or a technical mitigation we can commit to in the SOW.

Attachments: ByteGrid_SOW_v2.pdf (proposed SOW they sent).

Ask: can Eng/Platform evaluate feasibility + rough effort (sprint count) and whether we can/should treat as an exception for this deal vs. roadmap prioritization? If exception, we need guardrails and escalation path.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0127

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ByteGrid: enterprise ask — KV per-tenant isolation + route-level SLA (initial)

Thanks for the context Neha — high level thoughts: 

- Per-tenant KV isolation is doable but non-trivial. Depending on the runtime we can namespace caches, but we need to ensure eviction policies and memory accounting by tenant. That likely requires adding tenant-aware cache keys and metrics, plus some accounting in the autoscaler. Rough estimate: 3-4 sprints (two infra + two runtime) for MVP if we do it as internal feature work.

- Route-level SLA is more of an orchestration/routing layer enhancement: we already have routing policy hooks but not per-route SLO enforcement and automatic fallback to alternate model variants. MVP could be implemented as a policy service + a fallback table — 2-3 sprints. True hard SLOs (contract-backed) require deeper infra for capacity guarantees.

Question: is ByteGrid requesting hard SLA (financial penalties) or operational targets to be included in the SOW? That changes scope.

I can sketch a short RFC and a feasibility spike if you want.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ByteGrid: enterprise ask — KV per-tenant isolation + route-level SLA (initial)

Neha / Dev — quick operational constraints and options from Platform: 

1) KV isolation options:
   - "Soft" namespacing: prefix keys with tenant id. Low risk, low cost, immediate. Auditors may accept with attestation but not airtight for legal guarantees.
   - "Hard" isolation: dedicate cache instances or enforce per-tenant resource quotas + accounting. Higher cost and provisioning complexity; adds billing implications.

2) Route-level SLA: we can implement best-effort routing policies now. Contract-backed SLAs require reserved capacity (Dedicated) and capacity reservation windows + throttling policies. That ties into Dedicated product and changes billing/pricing.

If this is a deal-specific exception, propose: deliver soft namespacing + monitoring (1 sprint) + an addendum saying we will implement hard isolation on committed roadmap (6-8 weeks) with priority if customer signs. Platform can offer mitigation: configurable cache TTL and stricter eviction per-tenant.

I can make a pros/cons slide deck and map to infra tickets (INF-2148, INF-2152).

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Product Manager, Platform

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@bytegrid.io>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@bytegrid.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: ByteGrid: enterprise ask — KV per-tenant isolation + route-level SLA (initial)

Neha / team — thanks for the rapid responses. Clarifying: ByteGrid requires a contractual statement that our cached state for customer A will not be visible to customer B — auditors have asked for proof of isolation. We're open to an interim mitigation during procurement: an attestation + a timeline for hard isolation delivery, but we need a firm date in the SOW and minimum SLA language for latency (p95 < 200ms for core routes).

I've attached a redlined SOW and the procurement timeline. Our target is to sign by 6/10 to align with our audit window.

[Attachment: ByteGrid_SOW_v2.pdf]

— Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Security, ByteGrid

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ByteGrid: enterprise ask — KV per-tenant isolation + route-level SLA (initial)

Adding CS context — ByteGrid is at risk of not renewing if we can't give a reasonable mitigation. They value security controls highly (they're in fintech). My suggestion for an immediate path: 

- Offer a formal attestation letter signed by Redwood Security that outlines current isolation controls (namespacing, access controls, audit logs).
- Commit to delivering hard isolation (dedicated namespaces + per-tenant accounting) as a prioritized spike with a target delivery date of 6/30 (4 weeks).
- For SLA, offer a service-level objective in the SOW (non-financial at first) with the option to convert to a financial SLA once we have reserved capacity.

If Product/Eng can agree to a 6/30 target for hard isolation MVP (limited to Dedicated customers and gated by a signed SOW + deposit), this should get procurement over the goal line.

I will draft procurement-friendly language.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@bytegrid.io>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ByteGrid: enterprise ask — KV per-tenant isolation + route-level SLA (initial)

We can take this on as an exception with clear guardrails. Proposed plan: 

1) Deliver soft namespacing attestation immediately (this week) and provide the security questionnaire we already maintain (see attachment).
2) Kick a 2-week spike this week to validate design for hard isolation and put infra tickets (INF-2148, INF-2152). Goal: scope MVP for Dedicated-only deployment by 6/30.
3) For SLA: commit to an SLO (p95 < 200ms) for specified routes in SOW as a non-financial target. If customer requires financial SLA, move to a reserved capacity addendum and pricing discussion.

If sales can secure a signed SOW with a deposit, Eng will prioritize the spike and we will timebox deliverables. I will add an RFC and link tickets.

Next steps for Neha: confirm whether ByteGrid will sign with the deposit and whether they accept the non-financial SLO for now.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime
[Attachment: security_questionnaire_filled.pdf]
